description: This topic involves forming new words from given letters and arranging words or events in a meaningful or dictionary sequence. It tests a candidate's vocabulary and logical thinking abilities.

sections.title: Word Formation
sections.description: Forming new words using the letters of a given root word or checking which word cannot be formed from it.

cases.condition: When a word can be formed
results: Identify the letters present in the given root word.
Choose the option where all letters are available in the root word.
A letter must not be used more times than its frequency in the original root word.

cases.condition: When a word cannot be formed
results: Look for a letter in the given options that is completely absent in the root word.
Alternatively, find an option where a letter is used more times than it appears in the root word.

sections.title: Logical Sequence of Words
sections.description: Arranging given words in their natural, size-based, or chronological sequence.

key_concepts.explanation: Arranging objects or events logically from small to big, first to last, or lower to higher level.

steps.title: Understand the Relationship
steps.detail: Understand the exact meaning of each word and figure out how they are logically related to one another.

steps.title: Find a Logical Flow
steps.detail: Establish a natural progressive process (e.g., Seed -> Plant -> Tree -> Wood).

steps.title: Elimination from Options
steps.detail: Identify the logical first and last word of the sequence, and eliminate the multiple-choice options that do not match.

sections.title: Dictionary Order Arrangement
sections.description: Arranging words exactly as they would appear in a standard English dictionary.

steps.title: Compare the First Letter
steps.detail: Look at the first letter of all the given words and arrange them in alphabetical order from A to Z.

steps.title: Move to Next Letters
steps.detail: If the first letters of two or more words are identical, compare their second letters. If the second is also identical, move to the third, and so on.

steps.title: Exhaustion of Letters
steps.detail: If one word is entirely a part of another word (like 'CAR' and 'CART'), the shorter word will always come first in the dictionary.

sections.title: Jumbled Letters to Meaningful Word
sections.description: Placing scrambled or jumbled letters into the correct sequence to form a valid, meaningful English word.

steps.title: Identify Vowels and Consonants
steps.detail: Separate the vowels (A, E, I, O, U) and consonants from the given jumbled string to make it easier to recognize the word's structural pattern.

steps.title: Look for Prefixes or Suffixes
steps.detail: Try to identify common word endings (like '-TION', '-ING', '-MENT') or beginnings (like 'PRE-', 'UN-', 'DIS-').

steps.title: Use Option Codes
steps.detail: If number codes are given for each letter, place the letters in the sequence provided by the multiple-choice options to see which one forms a recognizable word.
